title: A Probabilistic Organization of Therapeutic Trajectory Evolution in Cancer Therapy
content: Persistent therapeutic variability remains a central challenge in cancer therapy despite increasingly precise molecular targeting, predictive biomarkers, and patient stratification. A previously developed state-space and trajectory-evolution framework interprets therapeutic outcome as an emergent consequence of trajectory evolution occurring within the state-space organization of the tumor–host system. However, a fundamental question remains unresolved: does a given initial state-space organization uniquely determine a therapeutic trajectory, or does it permit multiple dynamically accessible trajectory paths? Here, I develop a probabilistic extension of the state-space and trajectory-evolution framework. For a given initial state-space organization, denoted by θ0, and therapeutic input, denoted by μ, therapeutic evolution may be organized as a conditional probability distribution over dynamically accessible trajectories Ti, attractors Aj, and therapeutic outcomes yj: \[ P(T_i, A_j, y_j \mid \theta_0, \mu) \]. A highly concentrated distribution corresponds to near-deterministic trajectory evolution, in which one trajectory is overwhelmingly favored. By contrast, a distribution extending across multiple accessible trajectories provides the basis for stochastic therapeutic outcomes. Different initial state-space organizations define different but potentially overlapping probability distributions, allowing therapeutic trajectories to share downstream paths or converge toward the same attractor and therapeutic outcome. This formulation therefore provides a unified explanation for therapeutic variability, stochasticity, and convergence. State-space modulation can accordingly be interpreted as reorganization of the conditional probability distribution of therapeutic evolution. A state-space modulating operator, denoted by υ, transforms θ_0 into a modified state-space organization θυ, thereby altering the accessibility and relative probabilities of therapeutic trajectories and redirecting evolution toward modified attractors and outcomes: \[ \theta_0 \to \theta_v, \quad P(T_i, A_j, y_j \mid \theta_0, \mu) \to P(T_i', A_j', y_j' \mid \theta_v, \mu) \mathbb{I} \] This probabilistic formulation extends the state-space and trajectory-evolution framework by identifying therapeutic evolution as an organized conditional probability distribution over accessible trajectories, attractors, and outcomes.
